newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia issues first full fund manager licence.
newsitem.headline: Russia issues first full fund manager licence.

text.p: Pallada Asset Management has received full authorisation from Russia's Federal Commission for the Securities Market to manage mutual funds, a spokesman for the market watchdog said on Thursday.
He said Pallada is the first of nine licensed management companies, to receive full authorisation to manage a fund in this way, but several of the others have applied.
Pallada was founded by Boston Capital Management LLC, and Moscow power utility AO Mosenergo is a partner in the venture, he said.

The spokesman said Pallada intended to manage funds largely targeted at Russian middle-class investors, and so shares would be set at $100. The fund would initially focus on Treasury bills for investment.
Ordinary Russians currently have few possibilities to invest their savings, which many keep in cash at home, usually in dollars.
The authorities want to encourage a system of mutual funds to tap these savings, estimated at billions of dollars, but want to regulate the market to prevent frauds and scandals.
Many people lost money in a few well-publicised pyramid saving schemes in recent years.
